title: Spin Models
intro: Interacting qubits are described by spin Hamiltonians: sums of single-qubit fields and two-qubit couplings written in Pauli operators. The Ising, transverse-field Ising, XX and Heisenberg models are the standard ones, and the QRC reservoir is a disordered, all-to-all relative of them.

blocks.text: A spin model is a sum of local terms. Fields act on one qubit ($h_iZ_i$, $g_iX_i$), couplings on two ($J_{ij}\,P_iQ_j$ for Paulis $P$, $Q$). Which terms appear, on which pairs, and with what signs and randomness decides everything about the dynamics: what is conserved, how fast information spreads, whether the model can be solved exactly, and whether it makes a good reservoir.
The classical and the transverse-field Ising model

The Ising model couples neighbouring spins through $Z_iZ_{i+1}$ only. Every term is diagonal, so the eigenstates are just bit strings and nothing ever happens dynamically: it is a classical model written in quantum notation. Add a transverse field and it becomes the most-studied quantum spin model:

blocks.caption: The transverse-field Ising model on a chain.

blocks.text: The two terms compete. For $h \ll J$ the ground state is (nearly) all spins aligned in $z$, with a pair of almost degenerate ground states related by flipping every spin; for $h \gg J$ it is all spins along $+x$, with no $z$ order. In an infinitely long chain the change happens sharply at $h = J$, a quantum phase transition (Pfeuty 1970). The model conserves the global spin-flip parity $\prod_iX_i$, the analogue of the $Z$-parity of the QRC reservoir.

items: XX (flip-flop) coupling $X_iX_j + Y_iY_j$: moves an excitation from one spin to the other and conserves the total $Z$. A chain of these is a hopping model for one particle at a time.

Single $X_iX_j$ coupling: contains both flip-flop terms and pair creation ($\sigma^+\sigma^+ + \sigma^-\sigma^-$), so it changes the number of excitations by 0 or 2 and conserves only the parity. This is the coupling of the Fujii–Nakajima reservoir.
Heisenberg coupling $X_iX_j + Y_iY_j + Z_iZ_j$: rotationally symmetric, conserving the total spin in every direction.

blocks.text: Nearest-neighbour chains with only $XX$ and $YY$ couplings and $Z$ fields, the transverse-field Ising chain among them, map by the Jordan–Wigner transformation onto free fermions (Lieb, Schultz and Mattis 1961). Their dynamics can be computed classically with $2n\times2n$ matrices instead of $2^n\times2^n$ ones. They have many conserved quantities and are integrable. Adding longer-range couplings, randomness in the couplings, or a second field direction generally destroys this: the model becomes chaotic (ergodic), with level repulsion and fast scrambling.

The QRC reservoir is deliberately of the second kind. Its Hamiltonian $\sum_{i<j}J_{ij}X_iX_j + \sum_ih_iZ_i$ has random couplings on every pair, which breaks the free-fermion mapping and leaves parity as the only exact symmetry (The Spin-Network Reservoir (#/qrc/models/spin-network-reservoir)). Strong random fields push it back towards integrability by localising excitations, which is the trade-off explored on Dynamical Regimes (#/qrc/models/dynamical-regimes).

Output of the run, for an 8-spin open chain with $J = 1$: the end-to-end correlation $\langle Z_1Z_8\rangle$ in the ground state falls from 0.960 at $h = 0.2$ through 0.743 at $h = 0.5$ and 0.119 at $h = 1$ to essentially 0 at $h = 2$ and 5. The gap between the two lowest levels is tiny for small $h$ (0.0000 to four places at $h = 0.2$, the near-degenerate ordered pair) and opens up for large $h$ (2.19 at $h = 2$, 8.14 at $h = 5$). The product of all $X_i$ commutes with $H$.

blocks.title: Ground states without a field
blocks.text: For $H = -J\sum_i Z_iZ_{i+1}$ with $J > 0$ on 4 spins (open chain), what are the ground states and the ground energy?
solution: Each bond contributes $-J$ when its two spins agree and $+J$ when they differ.
All spins equal satisfies all 3 bonds: $\vert0000\rangle$ and $\vert1111\rangle$, energy $-3J$, a twofold degenerate ground state related by the global flip.

blocks.title: Counting couplings
blocks.text: How many random $J_{ij}$ does an all-to-all reservoir of 6 qubits have, and how many coupling terms does a 6-spin nearest-neighbour chain have?
solution: Open chain: 5 bonds. The all-to-all model's extra couplings are what break the free-fermion structure.

blocks.title: Which symmetry
blocks.text: Which of these is conserved by $\sum J_{ij}X_iX_j + \sum h_iZ_i$: total $Z$, the parity $\prod Z_i$, or the global flip $\prod X_i$?
solution: Total $Z$: no, $X_iX_j$ changes the excitation number by 2.
Parity $\prod Z_i$: yes, the change is always by an even number.
Global flip $\prod X_i$: it commutes with $X_iX_j$ but anticommutes with each $Z_i$, so not when $h \ne 0$.
